records.source: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שִׁמְר֥וּ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וַעֲשׂ֣וּ צְדָקָ֑ה כִּֽי־קְרוֹבָ֤ה יְשֽׁוּעָתִי֙ לָב֔וֹא וְצִדְקָתִ֖י לְהִגָּלֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: keep justice and do righteousness, for near [is] my salvation to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q Guard justice and practice righteousness, \q for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation is near and ready to come, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness is about to be made known.

L.1: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Keep justice and do righteousness, \q for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation [is] near to come, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness to be revealed.

R.1: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q Be fair to others and live in righteousness. \q Soon I will come to save you. \q Soon I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness to everyone.

decisions.choice: righteousness ... my righteousness: what God asks of his people answers to what he is about to do
decisions.reason: The same word is used first of the people's right conduct and then of God's own righteousness, shown in setting things right for his people. Because God is about to act, his people are to live in a way that fits his coming (46:13; 51:5-6).

decisions.choice: my righteousness: God's saving justice, his faithful act of putting things right
decisions.reason: Set beside "my salvation", the word means God's righteousness at work, rescuing his people and setting wrongs right (45:8; 46:13; 51:5).

decisions.choice: near to come: about to arrive
decisions.reason: The salvation is pictured as already on its way. The book's later chapters return to the same nearness (51:5; 62:11).

decisions.choice: Be fair to others; Soon I will come to save you
decisions.reason: Readable explains "keep justice" as fairness toward others and turns "my salvation is near to come" into a plain statement of what God will do.

records.heading: A house of prayer for all peoples

records.source: אַשְׁרֵ֤י אֱנוֹשׁ֙ יַעֲשֶׂה־זֹּ֔את וּבֶן־אָדָ֖ם יַחֲזִ֣יק בָּ֑הּ שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ וְשֹׁמֵ֥ר יָד֖וֹ מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת כָּל־רָֽע׃ס
records.gloss: How blessed [is the] person [who] does this, and [the] son of humankind [who] takes hold on it, [who] keeps [the] sabbath from profaning it, and [who] keeps his hand from doing any evil.
pieces: How blessed is the mortal who does this, \q the human being who clings to it, \q who guards the Sabbath and does not make it common, \q and who will not lift a hand to do any evil.

L.2: Blessed [is the] mortal [who] does this, \q and [the] {{gender:human being|son of man}} [who] holds fast to it, \q keeping [the] Sabbath from profaning it, \q and keeping his hand from doing any evil.

R.2: People who do this and hold on to it will be truly blessed. \q They keep the Sabbath day holy and do not treat it like an ordinary day. \q They do not do anything evil.

decisions.choice: blessed: in a happy and favored state
decisions.reason: The word describes the good life of someone who lives in God's way (30:18; 32:20; Psalm 1:1).

decisions.choice: keeping the Sabbath from profaning it: resting on the seventh day and not treating it as an ordinary working day
decisions.reason: The Sabbath was the sign of the covenant between God and Israel (Exodus 31:13-17). To profane it was to use it like any other day, for work and trade (Jeremiah 17:21-27; Nehemiah 13:15-22).

decisions.choice: this ... it: what verse 1 commands, keeping justice and doing right
decisions.reason: The pronouns point back to the commands of verse 1; the rest of the verse names two examples, keeping the Sabbath and avoiding evil.

decisions.choice: human being (setting: son of man)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "son of man" means any human being, parallel to "mortal". Literal gives the inclusive form by default, with the word-for-word form as a reader setting.

decisions.choice: keep the Sabbath day holy and do not treat it like an ordinary day
decisions.reason: Readable explains what profaning the Sabbath means.

records.source: וְאַל־יֹאמַ֣ר בֶּן־הַנֵּכָ֗ר הַנִּלְוָ֤ה אֶל־יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַבְדֵּ֧ל יַבְדִּילַ֛נִי יְהוָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל עַמּ֑וֹ וְאַל־יֹאמַר֙ הַסָּרִ֔יס הֵ֥ן אֲנִ֖י עֵ֥ץ יָבֵֽשׁ׃ס
records.gloss: And let not say the son of the foreignness who has joined himself to Yahweh, saying: surely he will separate me, Yahweh, from with his people; and let not say the eunuch: here! I [am] a tree dry.
pieces: The foreigner who has attached himself to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} must not say, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is sure to set me apart from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people." \q The eunuch must not say, \q "See, I am nothing but a dried-up tree."

L.3: And let not the foreigner who has joined himself to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will surely separate me from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people"; \q and let not the eunuch say, \q "Look, I [am] a dry tree."

R.3: Foreigners who have chosen to follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} should not say, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will surely keep me away from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people." \q And a eunuch, a man who cannot father children, should not say, \q "I am like a dead tree that can never bear fruit."

decisions.choice: the foreigner, the eunuch: two kinds of people the law kept out of the assembly of the LORD
decisions.reason: A eunuch is a castrated man, often an official at a royal court (39:7; 2 Kings 20:18). The law excluded such a man from the assembly of the LORD, and also excluded certain foreign peoples (Deuteronomy 23:2-9, which is 23:1-8 in many translations). The promise that follows overturns their fear.

decisions.choice: joined himself to the LORD: bound himself to the LORD by his own choice
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of foreigners joining Israel in 14:1 and of nations joining themselves to the LORD in Zechariah 2:15 (2:11 in many translations).

decisions.choice: a dry tree: a man with no children to carry on his name
decisions.reason: A tree that is dry bears no fruit. The eunuch fears that, with no descendants, his name will die with him. Verse 5 answers that fear.

decisions.choice: a eunuch, a man who cannot father children; a dead tree that can never bear fruit
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a eunuch is and what the picture of a dry tree means.

records.source: כִּי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לַסָּֽרִיסִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁמְרוּ֙ אֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתַ֔י וּבָֽחֲר֖וּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑צְתִּי וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh to the eunuchs who keep my sabbaths and choose [that] in which I delight and [are] holding fast to my covenant:
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this to the eunuchs who keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths, \q who choose what gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pleasure, \q and who hold firmly to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant:

L.4: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the eunuchs who keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths, \q and choose [that] in which I delight, \q and hold fast to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant:

R.4: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says to eunuchs who keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days, \q who choose to do what I want, \q and who are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant:

decisions.choice: my covenant: the covenant God made with Israel
decisions.reason: Holding fast to the covenant means keeping faith with the LORD and his commands. The Sabbath is called a lasting covenant in Exodus 31:16, so keeping it is a mark of belonging.

decisions.choice: my Sabbaths: the plural takes in every Sabbath
decisions.reason: The plural may mean each weekly Sabbath, as in Exodus 31:13, or include the other days of rest in Israel's calendar (Leviticus 23).

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֜ם בְּבֵיתִ֤י וּבְחֽוֹמֹתַי֙ יָ֣ד וָשֵׁ֔ם ט֖וֹב מִבָּנִ֣ים וּמִבָּנ֑וֹת שֵׁ֤ם עוֹלָם֙ אֶתֶּן־ל֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת׃ס
records.gloss: and I will give to them in my house and in my walls a monument and a name better than sons and than daughters; a name of perpetuity I will give to him, which will not be cut off.
pieces: within {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house and inside {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} walls I will set up for them a monument and a name worth more than sons and daughters. \q I will give each of them a name that lasts forever, \q one that will never be wiped out.

L.5: I will give to them in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house and within {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} walls a monument and a name better than sons and daughters; \q an everlasting name I will give to him, \q which will not be cut off.

R.5: I will give them a place in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house, inside {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} walls. They will be remembered there. \q That will be better than having sons and daughters to carry on their name. \q I will give them a name that will last forever. \q It will never be forgotten.

decisions.choice: a monument and a name: a lasting memorial, so that a person is not forgotten
decisions.reason: The word for monument is literally "hand". Absalom, who had no son, set up a pillar called his "hand" so that his name would be remembered (2 Samuel 18:18). Israel's memorial to the victims of the Holocaust, Yad Vashem, takes its name from this verse.

decisions.choice: my house and my walls: the temple and its courts
decisions.reason: The eunuch who might have been kept out of the assembly is given a place of honor inside God's own house (verse 7).

decisions.choice: to him: to each one of them
decisions.reason: The pronoun changes from plural to singular: each faithful eunuch receives his own lasting name.

decisions.choice: each of them
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the meaning decision on the singular pronoun; Literal keeps "him".

decisions.choice: They will be remembered there; to carry on their name
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the monument and name keep a person's memory alive, as children would.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י הַנֵּכָ֗ר הַנִּלְוִ֤ים עַל־יְהוָה֙ לְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ וּֽלְאַהֲבָה֙ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה לִהְי֥וֹת ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִ֑ים כָּל־שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And the sons of the foreignness who join themselves to Yahweh, to serve him and to love the name of Yahweh, to become his for servants, every [one who] keeps [the] sabbath from profaning it and [who are] holding fast to my covenant,
pieces: As for the foreigners who attach themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q who love the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and become {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants, \q everyone who guards the Sabbath and does not make it common \q and who clings to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant,

L.6: And the foreigners who join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and to love the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants, \q everyone who keeps [the] Sabbath from profaning it \q and holds fast to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant,

R.6: Foreigners may also join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q They serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, love the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and become {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants. \q They keep the Sabbath day holy and do not treat it like an ordinary day. \q They are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant.

decisions.choice: the sons of foreignness: foreigners, people of other nations
decisions.reason: "Son of" with a noun names a person of that kind. The same phrase is in verse 3.

decisions.choice: to serve him: to minister to him in worship
decisions.reason: The verb is often used of the service of priests and Levites (61:6; Deuteronomy 10:8). Here it may mean worship in general, or service at the temple itself (66:21).

decisions.choice: to be his servants: foreigners take the place Israel is given in these chapters
decisions.reason: Through chapters 40-55 Israel is the LORD's servant (41:8; 44:1). Here foreigners who love his name share that title.

records.source: וַהֲבִיאוֹתִ֞ים אֶל־הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֗י וְשִׂמַּחְתִּים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית תְּפִלָּתִ֔י עוֹלֹתֵיהֶ֧ם וְזִבְחֵיהֶ֛ם לְרָצ֖וֹן עַֽל־מִזְבְּחִ֑י כִּ֣י בֵיתִ֔י בֵּית־תְּפִלָּ֥ה יִקָּרֵ֖א לְכָל־הָעַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: and I will bring them to the mountain of my holiness and make them rejoice in the house of my prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices [will be] for acceptance on my altar; for my house a house of prayer it will be called for all the peoples.
pieces: I will lead them to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain and make them glad in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house of prayer. \q Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will find favor on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar, \q for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house will be named a house of prayer for all peoples.

L.7: and I will bring them to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain and make them rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house of prayer; \q their burnt offerings and their sacrifices [will be] accepted on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar; \q for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house will be called a house of prayer for all the peoples.

R.7: I will bring them to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will make them happy in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house, where people pray to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I will accept the burnt offerings and sacrifices they bring to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar. \q My house will be called a house of prayer for people of every nation.

decisions.choice: a house of prayer for all the peoples: the temple open to every nation
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes these words when he drives the traders out of the temple courts (Mark 11:17; Matthew 21:13; Luke 19:46). Mark keeps "for all the nations"; Matthew and Luke quote only "a house of prayer".

decisions.choice: my holy mountain: Mount Zion in Jerusalem, where the temple stood
decisions.reason: The mountain of the LORD's house is the place to which the nations come in 2:2-3 and 66:20.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and sacrifices: the whole offering burned on the altar, and the sacrifice shared in a meal
decisions.reason: The two words together cover the main kinds of animal offering (Leviticus 1; 3). That foreigners' offerings are accepted on God's altar shows they are fully received.

decisions.choice: in Jerusalem; where people pray to me
decisions.reason: Readable names the mountain and explains "house of prayer"; it says "people of every nation" for "all the peoples".

records.source: נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה מְקַבֵּ֖ץ נִדְחֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֛וֹד אֲקַבֵּ֥ץ עָלָ֖יו לְנִקְבָּצָֽיו׃
records.gloss: The utterance of [the] Lord Yahweh, [who] gathers the banished [ones] of Israel: still I will gather to it, to its gathered [ones].
pieces: So declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, who collects the scattered people of Israel: \q I will yet bring more to join them, beyond the ones already brought together.

L.8: [The] declaration of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, who gathers the outcasts of Israel: \q I will gather yet [others] to it, besides its gathered [ones].

R.8: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} gathers the people of Israel who were driven away. \q This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says: I will gather even more people and add them to those I have already gathered.

decisions.choice: the outcasts of Israel: Israelites driven out of their land and scattered
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of the exiles God will gather in 11:12; compare Deuteronomy 30:4 and Psalm 147:2.

decisions.choice: to it, besides its gathered ones: to Israel, in addition to the exiles already gathered
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to Israel. The ones God will add are most likely the foreigners of verses 3-7 (compare 66:18-21; John 10:16).

decisions.choice: The Lord GOD gathers ...; This is what he says
decisions.reason: Readable splits the verse into two sentences, putting the description of God first.

records.source: כֹּ֖ל חַיְת֣וֹ שָׂדָ֑י אֵתָ֕יוּ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל כָּל־חַיְת֖וֹ בַּיָּֽעַר׃ס
records.gloss: O every animal of [the] field, come to devour, O every animal in [the] forest!
pieces: Every creature that roams the fields, \q every beast in the forest, come here and devour!

L.9: All [you] beasts of [the] field, \q come to devour, all [you] beasts in the forest!

R.9: All you wild animals in the fields and forests, \q come and eat!

decisions.choice: wild animals called to devour: enemy nations invited to prey on an unguarded people
decisions.reason: The people are pictured as a flock left without protection, because its watchmen and shepherds fail (verses 10-11). Wild animals stand for hostile nations in Jeremiah 12:9 and Ezekiel 34:5, 8.

decisions.choice: come to devour: a summons spoken in bitter irony
decisions.reason: The call is a warning: since the leaders will not guard the people, nothing stands between them and those who would destroy them.

records.source: צֹפָ֞יו עִוְרִ֤ים כֻּלָּם֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ כֻּלָּם֙ כְּלָבִ֣ים אִלְּמִ֔ים לֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ לִנְבֹּ֑חַ הֹזִים֙ שֹֽׁכְבִ֔ים אֹהֲבֵ֖י לָנֽוּם׃
records.gloss: Its watchmen [are] blind, all of them; they do not know; all of them [are] dogs dumb, they are not able to bark, dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber.
pieces: The nation's lookouts are blind, every one; none of them understands. \q All of them are voiceless dogs that cannot give a bark; \q they sprawl out and dream, and dozing is what they love.

L.10: Its watchmen [are] blind; all of them do not know; \q all of them [are] mute dogs, \q [they] cannot bark, \q dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber.

R.10: The leaders who should watch over God's people are blind. None of them understands anything. \q They are like dogs that cannot bark to warn of danger. \q They just lie around and dream. \q All they want to do is sleep.

decisions.choice: watchmen: the people's leaders, prophets above all, whose task is to see danger and warn
decisions.reason: Prophets are called watchmen in Jeremiah 6:17 and Ezekiel 3:17; 33:7. A blind watchman cannot do the one thing he is there for.

decisions.choice: mute dogs: watchdogs that do not bark
decisions.reason: Dogs guarded flocks (Job 30:1). A dog that cannot bark gives no warning when the wild animals of verse 9 come.

decisions.choice: dreaming: lying in a stupor
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here, and its exact sense is uncertain. It may mean dreaming, or panting and raving in sleep. It sounds like the word for seers, perhaps a jab at prophets who see nothing.

decisions.choice: The leaders who should watch over God's people; like dogs that cannot bark to warn of danger
decisions.reason: Readable names who the watchmen are and explains the picture of the dogs.

decisions.choice: The nation's
decisions.reason: Balanced names the people meant by "its"; Literal keeps the pronoun.

records.heading: Blind watchmen and greedy shepherds

records.source: וְהַכְּלָבִ֣ים עַזֵּי־נֶ֗פֶשׁ לֹ֤א יָֽדְעוּ֙ שָׂבְעָ֔ה וְהֵ֣מָּה רֹעִ֔ים לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ הָבִ֑ין כֻּלָּם֙ לְדַרְכָּ֣ם פָּנ֔וּ אִ֥ישׁ לְבִצְע֖וֹ מִקָּצֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And the dogs [are] mighty of appetite; they do not know satiety; and they [are] shepherds; they do not know to understand; all of them to their own way have turned, each one to his own unjust gain, from his end.
pieces: The dogs are ravenous; they never know when they have had enough. \q And these are the shepherds! They have no discernment. \q They have all gone off their own way, \q every one of them grabbing what he can get.

L.11: And the dogs [are] strong of appetite; they do not know fullness; \q and they [are] shepherds; they do not know [how] to understand; \q all of them have turned to their own way, \q each one to his own gain, to the last [one].

R.11: These dogs are greedy and are never satisfied. \q And these are the leaders of God's people! But they do not understand anything. \q Each of them goes his own way. \q Every one of them is looking out only for himself and how to get rich.

decisions.choice: shepherds: the leaders and rulers of the people
decisions.reason: Kings and leaders are called shepherds who should care for the flock (Jeremiah 23:1-4; Ezekiel 34:2-10).

decisions.choice: and they are shepherds: the dogs and the shepherds are the same people
alternatives: and the shepherds, too, do not know how to understand
decisions.reason: The words can be read as an exclamation ("and these are the shepherds!") or as a plain statement that the shepherds, too, lack understanding. Either way, the greedy dogs are the people's leaders.

decisions.choice: his own gain: profit taken by force or fraud
decisions.reason: The word is used of dishonest gain (33:15; Jeremiah 6:13; Ezekiel 22:27).

decisions.choice: the leaders of God's people; looking out only for himself and how to get rich
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of shepherds and what "his own gain" means.

records.source: אֵתָ֥יוּ אֶקְחָה־יַ֖יִן וְנִסְבְּאָ֣ה שֵׁכָ֑ר וְהָיָ֤ה כָזֶה֙ י֣וֹם מָחָ֔ר גָּד֖וֹל יֶ֥תֶר מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: Come, let me take wine, and let us drink strong drink to excess; and it will be like this day, tomorrow, great, abundance exceedingly.
pieces: "Come on," they call, "I will bring the wine; let us soak ourselves in beer! \q Tomorrow will be like today, \q a grand day, with plenty and to spare."

L.12: "Come, let me get wine, and let us drink our fill of strong drink; \q and tomorrow will be like this day, \q great, [with] abundance beyond measure."

R.12: They say to each other, "Come on! I will get some wine. Let us drink beer until we are drunk. \q Tomorrow will be just as great as today, and even better!"

decisions.choice: come, let me get wine: the leaders' own words, quoted without introduction
decisions.reason: The change to "me" and "us" shows the shepherds of verse 11 speaking. They feast while their people are in danger (compare 22:13; 28:7).

decisions.choice: strong drink: beer or another fermented drink
decisions.reason: As in 5:11 and 28:7, the word names an intoxicating drink, most likely beer made from grain.

decisions.choice: they call; They say to each other
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speakers, since the Hebrew gives the words without saying who speaks.
